publication.title: SRA Search with real NCBI reads
publication.description: Real scientific computation through the AkôFlow daemon: 5 completed activities.
publication.readme:
# SRA Search: real sequencing reads

Adapt the [Pegasus SRA Search workflow](https://github.com/pegasus-isi/sra-search-pegasus-workflow) to five dependent/independent AkôFlow activities: build the reference index, acquire reads, align reads, package validated BAM results and render the measured alignment summary. The source revision and adaptations are recorded in `data/upstream.json`; upstream wrappers and their license are preserved in `scripts/upstream/`.

## Data and computation

The reference is the upstream crAssphage FASTA and the public accession is **SRR3403832**. Preparation fetches the complete paired FASTQ mirrors from ENA, verifies their published byte counts and MD5 digests, and records the ENA response in `data/read-provenance.json`. Reads are not subsampled. Acquisition uses ENA's FASTQ mirror of the same SRA accession rather than running the upstream `fasterq-dump` downloader.

The offline DAG decompresses both observations, builds the Bowtie2 reference index, aligns paired reads with Bowtie2, sorts and indexes the BAM with samtools, calculates flagstat/idxstats and packages BAM/BAI/reports. Bowtie2 is pinned to Debian's 2.5.0 build and samtools to 1.16.1; these differ from the current upstream container, so results are attributed to this declared toolchain.

## Prepare and run

Docker, Go and Python 3 are required. Allow at least 5 GiB free disk and 8 GiB RAM for the local profile; these are initial capacity recommendations rather than measured minimum requirements.

```sh
./prepare.sh
./run.sh
```

Preparation needs network access for the 224 MB compressed observations, Docker base and Debian tools. All five execution activities run in Docker without network access. `run.sh` validates complete real read processing and measured alignment counts, including legitimate zero-hit searches, BAM integrity, BAI access and every archived file hash. Outputs are `outputs/published-results.tar.gz`, `outputs/published-validation.json`, per-activity observations and the runner's manifest.

To submit the same DAG to your local AkôFlow daemon after preparation:

```sh
go run ../../tools/daemon-local -root ../.. -example scientific-workflows/sra-search -wait=false
```

Add `-api-url http://<daemon-host>:8080/akoflow-api` for a daemon bound to a LAN address. Configure `AKOFLOW_API_TOKEN` in the shell or pass the existing installation env file with `-env-file`.

## Validation status

This bundle is being prepared. A successful scientific execution and Hub receipt must be recorded before claiming validation or publication. No successful execution is inferred from the upstream documentation.

## Scientific result interpretation

This full human-gut sample can yield zero matches to the specific upstream crAssphage reference. Zero reference matches is a measured search outcome, not a failure of the alignment computation and not evidence about all organisms. Unmapped mates are retained in the sorted BAM so the report accounts for every processed observation. The final visualization is generated from the actual flagstat counts; it does not fabricate positive matches.

The final visualization activity also materializes `published-results.tar.gz` and `published-validation.json` as its own final outputs, preserving the BAM archive and validation report after intermediate workspace cleanup.
